o.text:
According to most etymologies, inherited from Proto-Turkic *(h)ōtčak or *ōtčuk (“fireplace”), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *(h)ōt (“fire”), whence Azerbaijani od (“fire”).
According to Clauson, from Proto-Turkic *očok, with the second vowel being rounded. The figurative senses are attested first in Ottoman Turkish in the 17th century.
Cognates
Cognate with Crimean Tatar ocaq, Turkish ocak, Kazakh ошақ (ošaq), Kyrgyz очок (ocok), Southern Altai очок (očok), Uzbek oʻchoq, Tatar учак (uçaq), Chuvash вучах (vuč̬ah), Bashkir уҫаҡ (ośaq). Russian оча́г (očág) and Armenian օջախ (ōǰax) are borrowed from Turkic.
Internationalism; from Russian сентя́брь (sentjábrʹ), ultimately from Latin September.
Borrowed from Arabic حَقِيقَةً (ḥaqīqatan), adverbial accusative of حَقِيقَة (ḥaqīqa). By surface analysis, həqiqət + -ən.
